headline: China keen to build Bangladesh-China-Myanmar Economic Corridor for regional cooperation
summary: China's Ambassador to Bangladesh, Yao Wen, announced the country's determination to establish the BCMEC, aiming to boost regional connectivity and economic ties. The project is open to other nations.
details: China is committed to constructing the Bangladesh-China-Myanmar Economic Corridor (BCMEC) to foster greater regional connectivity and economic cooperation, according to Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen. He emphasized that the project is solely focused on regional economic collaboration and is open to participation from other countries, including India.

The announcement follows Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's recent visit to China, during which Bangladesh and China agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a "shared future" community. The visit resulted in 17 MoUs and agreements covering areas such as the Global Development Initiative, a Chinese Special Economic Zone in Chattogram, and the modernization of Mongla Port.

During the visit, China also proposed a "2+2" dialogue on diplomatic and defense matters and discussed the BCMEC. Additionally, China pledged support for a joint feasibility study on the Teesta River management project. Ambassador Yao stated that the BCMEC could potentially aid in the repatriation of Rohingya refugees.

The BCIM Economic Corridor, initially proposed by China over a decade ago, had stalled due to a lack of interest from India. Regarding the security situation in Myanmar, Ambassador Yao indicated that China would collaborate with Myanmar's authorities.

On the Teesta River management project, Yao Wen explained its purpose is to improve the livelihoods of approximately 10 million people in northern Bangladesh, stating it is a bilateral cooperation between Bangladesh and China.

Ambassador Yao described the Prime Minister's visit as a "complete success" and a "milestone" that has elevated Bangladesh-China relations to a new strategic height, strengthening mutual trust. He also noted that defense cooperation is an integral part of the comprehensive partnership between the two nations, though he declined to comment on specific defense procurements.

headline_marked: Price of 12kg LPG cylinder [[drops by 357 taka]]
headline: Price of 12kg LPG cylinder drops by 357 taka
summary: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission has reduced the price of private sector LPG and auto gas, effective from this evening.
details: The price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from the private sector has decreased by 29.76 taka per kg. This results in a price drop of 357 taka for the most commonly used 12kg LPG cylinder, bringing its new price to 1,528 taka.
The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) announced the new prices on Thursday, which will take effect from 6 PM today.
BERC has set the price of LPG at 127.30 taka per kg, down from the previous price of 157.06 taka per kg. Prices for other cylinder sizes will be determined based on this rate.
The price of auto gas used in vehicles has also been reduced to 70.40 taka per liter, down from 86.93 taka per liter.
While the price of 12.5kg cylinders supplied by government companies remains unchanged at 825 taka, BERC continues to set prices monthly based on the Saudi Aramco contract price (CP).
The price reduction follows a decrease in the global market price of LPG after the cessation of conflict in the Middle East.
